media_work.title: Give Up Tomorrow
media_work.focus_or_theme: The controversial conviction of Paco Larrañaga in the Philippines for the kidnapping, rape, and murder of the Chiong sisters; judicial corruption; flaws in the justice system; the death penalty.
media_work.summaryNotes: Larrañaga had numerous witnesses testifying he was hundreds of miles away in Quezon City at the time of the crime in Cebu. Key prosecution witness Davidson Rusia's credibility was severely challenged.

media_item.focus_or_theme: The controversial conviction of Paco Larrañaga in the Philippines for the kidnapping, rape, and murder of the Chiong sisters; judicial corruption; flaws in the justice system; the death penalty.
media_item.summary_notes: This documentary focuses on the conviction of Paco Larrañaga in the Philippines, highlighting issues of judicial corruption, flawed justice systems, and the death penalty. It examines the alibi evidence presented and the controversial testimony of a key witness.

featured_individuals.sentence: Death penalty (later commuted to life imprisonment)
featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention with Homicide and Rape (Chiong sisters case)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Francisco Juan "Paco" Larrañaga was convicted in the Philippines for the kidnapping, rape, and murder of the Chiong sisters. He maintains his innocence and presented alibi evidence. He is currently serving his sentence in Spain.
contributing_factors_raw: Unreliable/questionable witness testimony (key witness Rusia admitted to prior convictions after denying them)
Limited ability for defense to cross-examine key witness
organizations_involved_raw: Likely human rights organizations and Spanish diplomatic efforts involved in his transfer.
